properties.name: Camp 14, Kaechon
properties.note: Total control zone where prisoners are never released. Shin Dong-hyuk (Escape from Camp 14) says he was born here.

properties.name: Camp 25, Chongjin
properties.note: Political prison camp on the edge of Chongjin. Satellite imagery showed new guard posts and buildings in the 2010s.

properties.name: Camp 15, Yodok
properties.note: Had a "revolutionizing zone" from which some prisoners were released, which is why most early camp testimony comes from here. Kang Chol-hwan (The Aquariums of Pyongyang) was held here as a child.

properties.name: Camp 16, Hwasong
properties.note: The largest known political prison camp, a few km from the Punggye-ri nuclear test site. Tens of thousands of prisoners estimated.

properties.name: Camp 22, Hoeryong
properties.note: Once one of the largest camps. Closed around 2012. What happened to its prisoners is unknown.

properties.name: Camp 18, Pukchang
properties.note: Mining camp across the river from Camp 14. Reports suggest it was closed or merged in the 2000s, though parts may still be used.

properties.name: Kyo-hwa-so No. 8, Yongdam
properties.note: Type of prisoners: Unknown Type of Labor: Unknown This location has not been confirmed by HRNK prisoner testimony. Both NKDB and KINU mention Yongdam as an unnumbered kyo-hwa-so located in Chonnae-gun, Kangwon Province. The 2011 NKDB volume, Prisoners in North Korea Today, lists a “Prison No. 8” located in the Seungho area of Pyongang. There is no further information about its current state of operation.

properties.name: Kyo-hwa-so No. 11, Chung-san
properties.note: Kyo-hwa-so No. 11, Chung-san is also transliterated as Chonsan, Jungsan, and Jeungsan.  500 Type of prisoners: Men, women, border crossers, political prisoners Type of Labor: Farming, construction, manufacturing Detailed analysis of Kyo-hwa-so No. 11, Chung-san can be found in this 2017 HRNK report: https://www.hrnk.org/uploads/pdfs/Hawk_The_Parallel_Gulag_Web.pdf

properties.name: Kyo-hwa-so No. 7, Kanggye
properties.note: Kyo-hwa-so No. 7, Kanggye is also transliterated as Kangkye and Ganggye.  Type of prisoners: Unknown Type of Labor: Unknown This location has not been confirmed by HRNK prisoner testimony. It has been listed in NKDB and KINU reports. There is no further information about its current state of operation.

properties.name: Kyo-hwa-so No. 2, Dongrim
properties.note: Type of prisoners: Unknown Type of Labor: Unknown This location has not been confirmed by HRNK prisoner testimony. It has been listed in NKDB reports in 2011 and 2016, as well as KINU reports in 2014 and 2016. There is no further information about its current state of operation. A second location associated with this camp known as Obong Workers' District is located at 39° 52’5.42”N 124° 44’59.35”E.

properties.name: Kyo-hwa-so No. 88, Wonsan
properties.note: Type of prisoners: Unknown Type of Labor: Unknown This location has not been confirmed by HRNK prisoner testimony. It has been previously listed in NKDB and KINU reports. There is no further information about its current state of operation. A second location associated with this camp is located in Chuksan-ri at 39° 11’57.43”N 127° 20’45.07”E

properties.name: Kyo-hwa-so No. 9, Hamhung
properties.note: Also transliterated as Hamheung, the 2011 NKDB report locates Kyo-hwa-so No. 9, Hamhung Men’s Prison at Hoeyang, Hoesang Area, Hamhung City, while Hamhung Women’s Prison is located at Songwon Village, which is also spelled as Sungwon, Hoesang Area, Hamhung City.  500 Type of prisoners: Men, women, political prisoners, forcibly repatriated women Type of Labor: Sewing, farming, gold mining A second location associated with this camp known as Hamhung Women's Prison is located in Sungwon-ri at 40° 3

properties.name: Sunchon Kyo-hwa-so
properties.note: Sunchon Kyo-hwa-so is sometimes known as Sukchon Kyo-hwa-so.  Type of prisoners: Unknown Type of Labor: Gold mining This location has not been confirmed by HRNK prisoner testimony. It has been listed in NKDB and KINU reports. There is no further information about its current state of operation.

properties.name: Kyo-hwa-so No. 8, Sungho-ri
properties.note: Type of prisoners: Unknown Type of Labor: Coal mining This location has not been confirmed by HRNK prisoner testimony. It has been previously listed in NKDB and KINU reports. There is no further information about its current state of operation. Detailed analysis of Kyo-hwa-so No. 8, Sungho-ri can be found in this 2019 HRNK report: https://www.hrnk.org/uploads/pdfs/Bermudez_Pokchongni_FINALFINAL_Web.pdf

properties.name: Facility at I-gol
properties.note: Type of prisoners: Unknown Type of Labor: Unknown This location has not been confirmed by HRNK prisoner testimony or listed by NGO reports. However, the satellite images share the appearance of other well documented kyo-hwa-so. There is no further information about its current state of operation.

properties.name: Facility at Udan
properties.note: Type of prisoners: Unknown Type of Labor: Unknown This location has not been confirmed by HRNK prisoner testimony or listed by NGO reports. However, the satellite images share the appearance of other well documented kyo-hwa-so. There is no further information about its current state of operation.

properties.name: Ch’oma-bong Restricted Area
properties.note: Type of prisoners: Unknown Type of Labor: Mining, agricultural production Detailed analysis of Ch’oma-bong Restricted Area can be found in this 2016 HRNK report: https://www.hrnk.org/uploads/pdfs/ASA_HRNK_Chmbg_201603_FINAL.pdf

properties.name: Kyo-hwa-so No. 3, Sinuiju
properties.note: Type of prisoners: Men, criminal offenders, political prisoners, other (uknown) Type of Labor: Rock and gold mining, prison uniform manufacturing This location is not yet confirmed. It has been listed in NKDB and KINU reports. There is no further information about its current state of operation.

properties.name: Kyohwaso No. 1, Kaechon
properties.note: Re-education prison for people convicted of crimes. Survivors describe forced labor and high death rates.

properties.name: Kyo-hwa-so No. 4, Kangdong
properties.note: Also transliterated as Gangdong, Kyo-hwa-so No. 4, Kangdong is located in Chael-kol on the eastern outskirts of Pyongyang close to South Pyongan Province.  to 4,000 Type of prisoners: Men, civilian and military offenders, political prisoners Type of Labor: Limestone and cement production Detailed analysis of Kyo-hwa-so No. 4, Kangdong can be found in this 2019 HRNK report: https://www.hrnk.org/uploads/pdfs/Bermudez_Kangdong_FINALFINAL.pdf

properties.name: Kyohwaso No. 12, Chongori
properties.note: Holds many people forcibly sent back from China after escaping. Testimony describes starvation and abuse, especially of women.

properties.name: Kyo-hwa-so No. 6, Sariwon
properties.note: to 4,000 Type of prisoners: Men, political prisoners Type of Labor: Clothing and Shoe factory, farming, "model detention facility" Kyo-hwa-so No. 6, Sariwon was one of the earliest North Korean prison camps to become widely known about outside of North Korea because of the involvement of Amnesty International in the release of Ali Lameda and Jacques Sedillot. They were members in good standing in the Venezuelan and French, respectively, communist parties. In 1967, both were recruited to Pyongyan

properties.note: It is believed that Kyo-hwa-so No. 22, Oro was closed around 2008.  Type of prisoners: Men, women, political prisoners, short term prisoners Type of Labor: Construction This location is not yet confirmed. It has been listed in NKDB and KINU reports as well as identified in prisoner testimony. There is no further information about its current state of operation. Type of prisoners: Men, political prisoners, genuine criminal offenders, border crossers Type of Labor: Gold mining This location is not yet confirmed.
